name: Max Saw: seven sawtooths after Adam Szabo's analysis of the Super Saw
description: model27's machine after Adam Szabo's analysis of the Super Saw (How to Emulate the Super Saw, KTH 2010; notes/84), written in fixed point on the EMAC: seven naive sawtooths, the centre at the note and six around it at Szabo's offsets times his detune curve, the centre's and the sides' levels from his two mix curves, a high-pass after them that follows the pitch, and a random phase for every sawtooth at each trig. Detune spreads the six (little up to the middle, then steeply); Mix goes from the centre alone to all seven, the two as loud at 95; Tone moves the high-pass against the fundamental, 16 steps an octave, Szabo's at 32, full below, thin above; Phase is how far the phases scatter at a trig, 127 fully random (Szabo's), 0 all seven together (a hard attack, then flanging). MACHINES + PUNCH switches Sub: an eighth oscillator, a sawtooth two octaves below the note through a low-pass at the note, as loud as a sine of height 1, added after the high-pass; the centre and the high-pass stay at the note (notes/84 §13). DECAY, GATE and PUNCH are the stock amp chain as on TONE; while the envelope is closed the voice stands still. Pitch as on every machine.

credit.who: Adam Szabo (How to Emulate the Super Saw, KTH 2010)

uses.why: Sub, a switch: bit 8 of k 32, which the voice reads in the note's sound every block (a trig's lock of k 32 at the trig); the shortcut layer flips and saves it

emulation.pattern: instructions a block, the whole voice loop less the same loop muted, note 60, DECAY 127 and default knobs unless named; the frame loops in assembly (maxsaw_cf.S); tools/emu/test_maxsaw.py, the maintainer's run of 2026-11-16 with the new Sub (notes/84 §14); before it 2 576 (§11), the C version 4 791 (§10.1)

changes: on its tracks, MACHINES held + PUNCH flips Sub instead of PUNCH, and the PUNCH LED shows the switch while MACHINES is held
unchanged: TRACK + PUNCH (Control All), with or without MACHINES

emulation.tool: the core against the same model in double on the host and the ColdFire object against the host build in a ColdFire interpreter (notes/84 §5, §7, §9); tools/emu/test_maxsaw.py (Unicorn, the OS's own code, against the host build tools/emu/maxsaw_ref.c, notes/84 §10): ALL OK, the core exact in 81 cases (13 758 blocks), the pause, Sub from the sound, a preview and a lock, the chain TONE's but the output stage, the tracks, next to SAMPLE and CHIPS; since notes/84 §11 the frame loops in assembly, the ColdFire interpreter: the object equal to the host core, the saturation's edges; the maintainer's Unicorn run of the assembly (core, chain, tracks, next, measure): ALL OK; since notes/84 §13 (the new Sub): the host core with Sub off equal to the core before, bit for bit; the Sub equal to the listening page's draft in double to 97.5 dB; the ColdFire interpreter: the object equal to the host core (six tracks, Sub switched), the Sub's loops at their edges; the maintainer's Unicorn run of the new Sub (core, chain, tracks, next, measure): ALL OK
emulation.build: alone, next to SAMPLE and next to CHIPS, composed by compose.py
